version.basis: K4 names only 'the NVIDIA Cosmos tokenizer (Agarwal et al., 2025)'. The checkpoint is the default of the authors' package gpi_pack (MIT, Copyright 2025 Kentaro Nakamura; repo commit 8836037), whose video module says it implements 'the representation used by the video paper', and whose documentation links 'NVIDIA Cosmos Tokenizer' to this checkpoint. The package also states the paper does not specify resize or frame-sampling policy. Exact version therefore = authors' package default, not a statement in the paper.

quotes.quote: NVIDIA Cosmos tokenizer (Agarwal et al., 2025) and extract their internal representations.
DEFAULT_COSMOS_MODEL_ID = "nvidia/Cosmos-1.0-Tokenizer-CV8x8x8"
For each segment, the representation used by the video paper is the Cosmos decoder input (``vae.post_quant_conv(latent)``) averaged over its latent-time axis.
This section describes how to do so using the `NVIDIA Cosmos Tokenizer <https://huggingface.co/nvidia/Cosmos-1.0-Tokenizer-CV8x8x8>`_.
The paper reports a `(16, 40, 60)` representation, but does not specify its resize or frame-sampling policy

compute.basis: Order of magnitude only. (i) Card runtime 34.8 ms/frame (A100, encode+decode, 720x1280, 105M 4x8x8 CV proxy) scaled by pixel count to 320x480 and by the dense-BF16 peak ratio A100 312 / RTX 4500 Ada 158.5; encode-only taken as half (assumption). (ii) The 052590c conv-VAE calibration c*P*voxels with P = 105M (whole-AE proxy) at 30% of dense BF16 peak. The representation needs only encode + post_quant_conv (no decode). Frame decoding is dense: <=121 of the 125 (25 fps), 150 (30 fps) or 250 (50 fps) native frames per 5-s segment are selected uniformly, so every native frame must be decoded. Native-resolution input (frame_size=None, the package default) would cost about 13.5x more at 1080p.
